meta.title: Finance Scraper — invest with fundamentals
meta.description: A free, open-source tool that turns financial data into clear reports for learning about and researching companies.
hero.accessible_phrases: Invest with fundamentals, clarity, and at your own pace.
hero.summary: Finance Scraper turns financial data into clear, visual, free reports to help you research a company before making a decision.
intro.title: The stock market can be understood one step at a time.
intro.description: {{app_name}} is a free, open-source tool that brings together information about listed companies and presents it visually, so you can explore the fundamentals without prior experience.
intro.callout: A place to start asking better questions, not a signal to buy or sell.
features.title: From scattered numbers to a story you can follow.
features.description: Each view helps put the data in context. The final decision is always yours.
features.card1.title: Data with context
features.card1.description: Review revenue, earnings, and other fundamental indicators to better understand a company's journey.
features.card2.title: Valuation without shortcuts
features.card2.description: Explore valuation metrics and compare them with the available information without turning a number into a recommendation.
features.card3.title: A company, not just a ticker
features.card3.description: Explore company information and market signals to understand the business behind a ticker symbol.
report.title: Fewer endless tables. More clarity.
report.description: Finance Scraper organizes financial data into a view you can explore without being a specialist. Start with a question, follow the indicators, and build your own perspective.

audience.adults.title: Adults

globe.title: One planet. Dozens of paths. Connected markets.

globe.disclaimer: These routes are random illustrations, not real transactions. Finance Scraper does not place trades or affiliate with brokers.
why.title: From a private tool to an idea worth sharing.
why.story1: Finance Scraper began as a private tool for analyzing publicly traded companies and exploring potential investments as a hobby. It was a personal way to follow a curiosity, bring together data scattered across websites, spreadsheets, and lengthy reports, and learn to read the numbers before making a decision.
why.story2: Its direction changed when the idea was presented as a school project for Reto STEAM, a competitive platform hosted by Recrea Jalisco, Mexico. The program brings together Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Maths to solve real problems with creativity and knowledge. What began as a tool for one person started to look like a way to bring more students and families closer to financial analysis.
why.story3: That sparked a bigger ambition: turning a private tool into a free, open-source project that welcomes improvements and people with different levels of experience. Finance Scraper aims to help anyone explore fundamentals, ask better questions, and build their own view of a company, without promising returns or telling them what to buy.
